checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in CO
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications
ADA fixture counts per IBC Table 2902.1 + 60 in turning radius + lavatory pipe wrap insulation per ADA §606.5 + mirror reflective edge ≤40 in AFF per ADA §603.3
Walk-in cooler envelope per IECC 403.10.1 (≥R-25 medium-temp panels, ≥R-32 freezer panels); door gasket seal verification at final
Existing sprinkler system reuse: hydraulic recalc for new layout + current 5-year cert per NFPA 25; new heads in cooking equipment area must be K-25+ per NFPA 13
Fire alarm + emergency lighting per NFPA 72/101 with current battery capacity test on file
Change of occupancy memo (B/M → A-2): include occupant load + exits + restroom count + sprinkler/fire-alarm impacts per IEBC §1001.2/1001.3 + IBC §303.3 (Group A-2)
Outdoor patio / sidewalk dining: verify city zoning (use permit may apply, e.g. Phoenix ZO §1207); include patio in occupant load + exiting + accessible route + sprinkler/awning review

Phoenix-specific (or equivalent local rule): contractor must be AZ ROC licensed AND associated with the Phoenix SHAPE PHX permit account before submittal (A.R.S. Title 32 Ch. 10) — frequently-missed pre-submittal blocker
Reject token min-fee outputs; calculate from the live fee schedule before quoting

Confirm the required license is active and matches the application: Licensed commercial contractors pull the permits for their trade scope, and Denver requires Denver-licensed electricians for electrical work. The contractor's license number must appear on the application. For this job, the electrical permit should be pulled by a Denver-licensed electrician or electrical contractor; plumbing and mechanical permits should be pulled by the appropriate licensed trade contractor on the project.
Bring 2 copies of all documents to City and County of Denver Community Planning and Development (CPD)
response_body.city_contractor_registration: Denver requires city-level contractor licensing/registration for electrical work in addition to the Colorado state electrical license. Verify the Denver electrical license is current before submitting the electrical permit. For other trades, confirm whether the contractor is properly registered with Denver CPD for commercial permit filing before application submission.

common_mistakes: Submitting the permit application without verifying current Denver contractor registration status — an expired or lapsed city registration will block the application silently
Treating the brewery TI as a simple trade permit job when the building permit and plan review are required for the tenant finish scope
Forgetting that floor drains need plumbing permit coverage for trap, vent, and sanitary tie-in details, not just a building permit
Installing gas-fired equipment without a mechanical permit covering venting, combustion air, and gas appliance clearances
Starting electrical work before confirming the electrician is Denver-licensed and listed on the permit application
Missing fire/life-safety or accessibility review items in a commercial tenant improvement, which can trigger correction cycles and delay occupancy

pro_tips: Use Denver's online CPD portal instead of walking paper plans in — Denver's online permit portal often moves faster than in-person submissions
For a brewery TI, submit coordinated MEP sheets together so plan review does not bounce the job between building, plumbing, mechanical, and electrical reviewers
Have equipment cut sheets ready before intake; commercial reviewers will want gas input, venting, electrical load, and clearances up front
Check your Denver contractor registration renewal date before starting any permit application — registration lapses are one of the most avoidable rejection reasons
If the project value is already $420,000, expect valuation-based fees and plan review charges to be material; budget time for corrections rather than assuming quick permit treatment

what_to_bring: Completed commercial tenant improvement permit application and project address
Signed tenant improvement plans showing floor drains, gas-fired equipment, and electrical scope
Equipment cut sheets for all gas-fired equipment and fermentation tanks with utility requirements
Plumbing riser/drainage details for floor drains, trap primers, and sanitary tie-ins
Electrical load information, panel schedule, and one-line diagram if new circuits or service changes are involved
Contractor license numbers and Denver registration information for each trade pulling permits
response_body.zoning_hoa_flag: For a brewery tenant improvement in Denver, zoning and use approval can matter if the space is changing use intensity, adding exterior equipment, rooftop penetrations, odor/noise-producing exhaust, or signage. Historic district overlays, downtown design review, and occupancy/use restrictions may also apply. HOA issues are usually not the main issue for a commercial tenant space, but landlord approval and lease conditions often are.
